summary: Representative Kennedy has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about protecting children from human-like chatbots, a federal AI regulatory sandbox modeled on Utah's, using AI to speed up scientific research, and competing with China.

Representative Owens has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about preparing colleges and students for AI, keeping parents and teachers in charge of AI in schools, and AI investment and jobs.

Representative Wittman has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about AI as a matter of national security and strategic advantage, the energy supply it needs, the costs of data centers, and protecting children from deepfakes.

Representative Kiggans has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about a bill for a national strategy on American AI leadership, saying AI "will define the next century of economic growth, national security, and global competitiveness", and about data center grid costs.

Representative Scott has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI call for Congress to set rules on AI in schools, workplaces and health care, citing bias in hiring tools, worker surveillance, child safety and privacy, and oppose blocking state AI laws.

Representative McClellan has acknowledged that AI could threaten humanity. They have called for action "before the quest for profit ends humanity" and relayed a former Anthropic employee's warning that AI could "kill us all by the end of the decade." They also co-signed letters seeking oversight of frontier AI companies.

Representative McGuire has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about keeping data center grid costs off household bills, power supply for AI and winning the AI race against China, including asking how "AI superintelligence might actually help us solve the energy problem".

Representative Cline has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Asked about researchers' warnings on advanced AI, they called for safeguards such as "a third-party observer who can monitor that kind of development" and said AI companies should be liable for harm. Their other AI statements are about data center costs and defense.

Representative Vindman has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed warns of "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons." Their own statements on AI are about making data centers pay for their electricity.

Representative Beyer has acknowledged existential risk from AI. They called the "existential warnings from the experts building this technology" a wake-up call and have spoken of "potential systemic and civilizational risks" from AI. Beyer also led a letter urging House leaders to act "before true catastrophes occur".

Representative Griffith has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are mostly about health care, where they wrote "A blanketed embrace of AI technologies without appropriate guardrails would be irresponsible", and about data center electricity and water costs and political bias in chatbots.

Representative Subramanyam has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed warns of "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons." They have themselves raised concern about "an AI model getting out and going a little crazy and doing a lot of harm".

Representative Walkinshaw has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed warns of "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons." They have themselves cited "very serious cyber security and safety risks posed by advanced AI" and called for AI talks with China.

Representative Balint has acknowledged that AI could threaten humanity. They have said AI companies must not "literally gamble with the future of humanity" and criticized "letting billionaires play with the safety of humanity." Their other AI statements are about deepfakes, addictive chatbots and the power of AI companies.

Representative DelBene has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed warns of "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons." In their own words, they have called for guardrails against "the threat AI poses", citing its builders, and criticized AI denials in Medicare.

Representative Larsen has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI call for AI regulation and public education and for Congress to get serious about AI, and mock executive orders written with AI.

Representative Gluesenkamp Perez has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about a child safety law for AI chatbots, chatbots sending explicit material to children, and farmland bought for data centers.

Representative Newhouse has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about expanding electricity supply for AI data centers so that the United States, not China or other rivals, leads in AI.

Representative Baumgartner has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about winning the AI race while making data centers pay their own power and water costs, and about how foreign adversaries use generative AI, which an amendment they offered called a possible "national security risk".

Representative Jayapal has acknowledged that AI could threaten humanity. Relaying industry researchers' warnings that "AI could destroy humanity", they wrote "Congress needs to act", and they have proposed making illegal "AI models that can go rogue, create catastrophic risks".

Representative Schrier has acknowledged existential risk from AI. They have urged Congress to act on "this existential threat now". Their other AI statements are about doctors rather than AI making insurance decisions and federal rules to protect consumers.

Representative Smith has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about AI in Medicaid preauthorization, mental health guardrails for chatbots and jobs, and include a call for US-China talks on controlling AI that names no risk.

Representative Strickland has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI promote the AI industry, including at a forum on federal AI policy and support for Black entrepreneurs, where they said "Washington state is a leader in the AI industry".

Representative Steil has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about financial regulation, saying "Regulators must evolve as quickly as the technologies that they oversee", and about the economy, jobs, energy costs and data centers.

Representative Pocan has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about labor standards for workers, AI in Medicare prior authorization, deceptive AI videos, and votes for data center tax breaks and against state AI regulation.
Representative Van Orden has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The only relevant posts found are about data centers being built on farmland, used in attacks on a political opponent.

Representative Moore has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about how the IRS and Social Security use AI, including concern that it will lead to denied or delayed benefits, and about data center projects.

Representative Fitzgerald has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. They favor a light-touch approach, warning that some in government want to regulate "before they even understand what they are regulating". Other AI statements are about likeness protections, data center electricity costs and competition with China.

Representative Grothman has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. They have said AI brings "serious risks if it’s not handled responsibly" without naming them; their other AI statements are about AI in classrooms and workplaces, jobs, privacy and data center electricity costs.
Representative Tiffany has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. No public statement by Representative Tiffany on the risks, benefits or regulation of AI was found.
Representative Wied has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about leading the AI race, privacy, and where data centers are built.

Representative Moore has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about its effects on workers, calling it "potentially the nuclear bomb for work as we know it", and about keeping data center electricity costs off household bills.
Representative-elect Amish Shah has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The only relevant statements found are about the water and power used by data centers during a drought.
Representative-elect Mark Lamb has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The only relevant statements found are about the strain data centers put on Arizona's water, power and infrastructure.

Representative-elect Eric Jones has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The only relevant statement found calls for regulating AI and protecting people, without naming a serious danger from AI.

Representative-elect Scott Wiener has acknowledged that AI could escape human control and threaten humanity. They have warned that recursive self-improvement is "potentially a recipe for total loss of control", endorsed a statement on "the risk AI presents to humanity", and pushed legislation requiring AI labs to address catastrophic risks.

Representative-elect Randy Villegas has acknowledged that AI could threaten humanity. They wrote "We cannot allow AI to displace workers, and threaten life, jobs and humanity." Their other AI statements are about a data center moratorium in the Central Valley and protecting personal data and jobs.

Representative-elect Angela Gonzales-Torres has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about AI industry campaign money and influence in politics, and opposition to data centers.
Representative-elect Marni von Wilpert has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The only relevant statement found is about a local data center's effect on housing, costs and jobs.

Representative-elect Melat Kiros has acknowledged that AI could escape human control. They warned that if AI reaches superintelligence without guardrails, "we’ll be as significant to them as ants are to us", and called for a pause over "the threat of a technology we can’t control".
